headline: Last session: Top firms' mcap surges Rs 3.65 lakh cr as TCS shines; FPIs withdraw Rs 52,100 cr

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 19 October.

why: FPIs pulled out Rs 52,100 crore from equities in October due to global headwinds
Nine of the top-10 most valued firms added Rs 3.65 lakh crore to their market capitalization
HDFC Bank reported a surge in credit card issuances, adding 14 lakh cards in three months
IT firms like TCS and Wipro are adjusting hiring and salary strategies as AI reshapes the workforce
whatHappening: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) continue to sell Indian equities amid global economic pressures
TCS emerged as a top performer in terms of market valuation gains during the last session
HDFC Bank is seeing aggressive expansion in its credit card segment
The IT sector is experiencing a shift in workforce management and salary hike policies
summary: On the last trading day, major Indian firms saw a significant market cap increase led by TCS. However, FPIs have withdrawn over Rs 52,100 crore in October amid global headwinds. HDFC Bank reported strong growth in its credit card business with 14 lakh new issuances.
